How these numbers were obtained: file size, dimensions, CRS, bands, compression and pixel spacing come directly from the GeoTIFF headers. Meter-scale pixel size was calculated from the geographic pixel spacing at the image latitude. Footprint and overlap areas were calculated from the GeoTIFF alpha bands at preview resolution, so they are labelled approximate—not survey-authoritative area measurements.

Are all GSD values the same?No. The output pixels range from 0.884 to 0.910 cm—a 2.9% spread. They are close enough to describe as approximately 0.9 cm, but the exact values should remain in the inventory.
GSD versus output pixel sizeThe final TIFF records raster pixel spacing, not the original camera flight GSD report. Therefore this inventory uses “output pixel size.” Flight GSD should come from the photogrammetry processing report if available.
RGBA, 8-bitBands 1–3 are red, green and blue. Band 4 is alpha transparency, which separates valid orthomosaic pixels from empty image edges.
EPSG:4326The orthomosaics are stored in geographic longitude/latitude coordinates. A metric project CRS such as UTM 48S may be preferred for precise distance, area and merging work.
LZW tiled GeoTIFFAll five files use lossless LZW compression, 256 × 256 pixel tiles and internal overviews. These properties support efficient GIS viewing despite the large files.
Accuracy not in the TIFFGround-control/checkpoint RMSE and camera-calibration accuracy are not present in the GeoTIFF headers. Those values must come from the original photogrammetry quality report.

Pending
Important for the 22–23 merge: the two images were acquired on different days. Water level, waves, illumination and color can differ across the overlap. A geometry merge is possible, but the seamline and radiometric consistency must be checked. Keep a source/date index so every output pixel remains traceable to 22 or 23 June.
Visual QCCheck missing areas, black/transparent gaps, duplicate objects, warped shoreline, blurred patches, seamlines, exposure shifts and moving boats.
Geometric QCCompare stable features in overlaps and, if available, report GCP/checkpoint RMSE. Do not infer positional accuracy from pixel size.
Delivery optimizationKeep original files unchanged. Produce final merged/separate outputs as tiled Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs with overviews and clear metadata.

5. What should be shown for the orthomosaic?

A concise reporting checklist for the lab head or professor.

1
One complete coverage mapShow all five outputs over an Esri basemap, with layer switches and clear labels for the 22–23 combined block and the three separate 24 June FMs.
2
One full preview per outputShow the complete footprint and transparent edges. State that previews are reduced resolution and originals are GeoTIFFs.
3
Output pixel size—not only “GSD”Report the measured 0.884–0.910 cm range, plus the approximate 0.9 cm summary. Add flight GSD only if found in the processing report.
4
Core technical metadataDate, FM unit, filename, dimensions, file size, CRS, color bands, alpha band, compression and valid footprint area.
5
Merge decision and provenanceExplain that 22 and 23 June overlap and will form one product; 24 June FM1–FM3 remain separate. Preserve source-date traceability.
6
Full-resolution QA samplesAdd 100% crops at reef texture, shoreline/structures, overlap seam and outer edge to demonstrate sharpness, alignment and gaps.
7
Photogrammetry accuracyReport GCP/checkpoint RMSE and processing settings only from the original quality report. These values cannot be recovered from the final TIFF header.
8
Preprocessing statusClearly separate “orthomosaic generated” from “merge complete,” “QC complete” and “final delivery ready.”
